title: Part 1 - An Introduction to ICD-11 / International Classification of Diseases (ICD)
subject: International Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD)
object: recording, reporting and grouping conditions and factors that influence health
context: Part 1 opening; purpose is systematic recording, analysis, interpretation and comparison of mortality and morbidity data; WHO role in maintenance legally mandated by the WHO International Nomenclature Regulations
evidence_wording: The International Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems (ICD) is a tool for recording, reporting and grouping conditions and factors that influence health. ... The purpose of the ICD is to allow the systematic recording, analysis, interpretation and comparison of mortality and morbidity data collected in different countries or regions and at different times.

title: Intended uses
subject: ICD
object: a broad range of use cases (causes of death, morbidity, epidemiology, casemix, quality and patient safety, primary care, functioning assessment, research, prevention, substance or device safety, surveillance, cancer registration, injury research, semantic interoperability)
context: where innovative uses of ICD are envisaged, it is recommended to consult with the WHO
evidence_wording: The ICD has been designed to address the needs of a broad range of use cases, such as: causes of death, morbidity, epidemiology, casemix (Diagnosis-Related Groups (DRG)), quality and patient safety, primary care, functioning assessment, research, prevention, substance (medication) or device safety, specific surveillance like antimicrobial resistance (AMR), cancer registration, injury research, as well as ensuring semantic interoperability for clinical documentation, decision support and guidelines or recommendations.

title: Classification
subject: classification
object: an exhaustive set of mutually exclusive categories to aggregate data at a pre-prescribed level of specialisation for a specific purpose
context: coding rules must be incorporated in the classification to achieve consistency of coding and comparability; classifications are complementary to terminologies
evidence_wording: A classification is “an exhaustive set of mutually exclusive categories to aggregate data at a pre-prescribed level of specialisation for a specific purpose” (ISO 17115). ... Coding rules must be incorporated in the classification to achieve consistency of coding and comparability of coded data over time and place.

title: ICD in the context of the WHO Family of International Classifications (WHO-FIC)
subject: WHO Family of International Classifications (WHO-FIC)
object: three broad groups: Reference classifications, Derived classifications, and Related classifications
context: Reference and Derived classifications are based on the Foundation Component; purpose of WHO-FIC is to assist development of reliable statistical and other data systems
evidence_wording: The WHO Family of International Classifications (WHO-FIC) comprises classifications that have been endorsed by the WHO to describe various aspects of health and the health system in a consistent manner. The WHO-FIC provides standardised building blocks for health information systems and consists of three broad groups: Reference classifications, Derived classifications, and Related classifications.

title: Figure 1: Relationships between the WHO Family of International Classifications (WHO-FIC) and Related Classifications, the Foundation Component, and shared terms
subject: Figure 1 (WHO-FIC relationships diagram)
object: relationships between the WHO-FIC and Related Classifications, the Foundation Component, and shared terms
context: figure caption only; image content not distillable from text layer
evidence_wording: Figure 1: Relationships between the WHO Family of International Classifications (WHO-FIC) and Related Classifications, the Foundation Component, and shared terms.

title: WHO-FIC: Reference Classifications
subject: WHO-FIC reference classifications
predicate: cover the main parameters of the health system and are
object: ICD, ICF, ICHI; approved and recommended as standards for international reporting on health
context: based on the same Foundation Component and share sets of Extension Codes; products of international agreements
evidence_wording: Reference classifications cover the main parameters of the health system, such as death and disease (ICD), disability, functioning, and health (ICF) and health interventions (ICHI). ... The three Reference classifications are: 1. International Classification of Diseases and Health Related Problems (ICD) 2. International Classification of Functioning, Disability & Health (ICF) 3. International Classification Health Interventions (ICHI). The Reference Classifications are based on the same Foundation Component and share sets of Extension Codes.

title: International Classification of Functioning, Disability & Health (ICF)
subject: ICF
object: measuring health and functioning/disability at both the individual and population levels
context: ICF classifies in two parts: functioning and disability (Body functions and structures; Activities and participation) and contextual factors (Environmental factors; Personal factors); ICF codes are only complete with a qualifier denoting level of health/severity
severity_qualifier: qualifier denotes level of health (severity of the problem from 'no problem' to 'complete problem')
exception_condition: the ICF and the codes within it do not confer an international binary status of disabled/not disabled; personal factors not classified in ICF due to large social and cultural variants
evidence_wording: The ICF is the WHO’s framework for measuring health and functioning/disability at both the individual and population levels. While the ICD classifies diseases and causes of death, the ICF classifies health and health-related domains. ICD and ICF together provide a framework to capture the full picture of health. ... ICF codes are only complete with the presence of a qualifier, which denotes the level of health (i.e. severity of the problem from ‘no problem’ to ‘complete problem’). Without qualifiers, codes have no inherent meaning.

title: ICF component definitions (functioning and disability terms)
subject: ICF descriptive terms
object: body functions, body structures, impairments, activity, activity limitations, participation, participation restrictions, environmental factors; ICF code domains b/s/d/e
context: disability is an umbrella term for impairments, activity limitations and participation restrictions; disabilities envisioned as a continuum
evidence_wording: Disability is an umbrella term for impairments, activity limitations and participation restrictions. ... ICF includes codes for Body Functions (b), Body Structures (s), Activities and Participation (d), and Environmental Factors (e).

title: The International Classification of Health Interventions (ICHI)
subject: ICHI
object: all functional sectors of the health system (acute care, primary care, rehabilitation, assistance with functioning, prevention, public health, ancillary services)
context: ICHI coding system comprises a seven-character category structure for the three axes Target (3 letters), Action (2 letters), Means (2 letters); not every possible combination is a valid ICHI domain; development began in 2007
exception_condition: devices not included as an axis (may be included as extension codes); drugs or other substances administered through an intervention are classified elsewhere (e.g. ICD, ATC/DDD, INN)
evidence_wording: ICHI includes interventions across all functional sectors of the health system, covering acute care, primary care, rehabilitation, assistance with functioning, prevention, public health, and ancillary services. ... The coding system comprises a seven-character category structure for the three axes: Three letters for the Target, Two letters for the Action, Two letters for the Means.

title: WHO-FIC: Derived classifications
subject: WHO-FIC derived classifications
object: national or international level or for a particular specialty, based on reference classifications (ICD, ICF, ICHI)
context: may be prepared by adopting the reference classification structure and classes, providing additional detail, or rearrangement/aggregation of items; ICD-11 has specialty linearisations for dermatology, primary care and mental health
evidence_wording: Derived classifications are often tailored for use at the national or international level or for use in a particular specialty. They are based on reference classifications (i.e. ICD, ICF, ICHI). ... ICD-11 has specialty linearisations that are derived from the common foundation. These include a version for dermatology, one for primary care and one for mental health. Others may follow.

title: Related classifications
subject: WHO-FIC related classifications
object: important aspects of health or the health system not covered by reference or derived classifications: ICPC, ICECI, ISO9999, ATC/DDD, ICNP
evidence_wording: Related classifications are included in the WHO Family of International Classifications to describe important aspects of health or the health system not covered by reference or derived classifications. Related classifications are: International Classification of Primary Care (ICPC); International Classification of External Causes of Injury (ICECI); Technical aids for persons with disabilities (ISO9999); The Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical Classification with Defined Daily Doses (ATC/DDD); The International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP).

title: ICD use in health information systems
subject: health information systems
object: collection, analysis, and use of health data; standardisation of coding enables intra- and international data comparison if the same coding rules are applied
context: population-based sources: CRVS systems, census data, household surveys; facility-related: surveillance, RHIS, health system monitoring, National health accounts (NHA)
evidence_wording: Health information systems are increasingly based on digital (electronic) reporting and coding. ICD–11 is designed to be used in such environments. The content of this Reference Guide is the only additional document required when coding with ICD-11. ... ICD coded data can be compared across different sectors of the health system – if the same coding rules are applied.

title: Use of ICD-11 in a digital setting and with web services
subject: ICD-11 digital use
predicate: is used for coding of diagnoses in
object: electronic health records, electronic death certificates, or other digital data collections
context: ICD-11 Coding Tool facilitates finding codes; retaining the unique identifier allows reuse across translations; WHO ICD web services at https://icd.who.int/icdapi
evidence_wording: ICD-11 is used for coding of diagnoses, in electronic health records or with electronic death certificates, or in other digital data collections. ... Retaining the unique identifier of the coded ICD-11 entity allows the same information to be reused across different translations.

title: Use of ICD-11 in an analogue paper-based setting
subject: paper-based ICD-11 use
object: manual transcription into electronic systems; consideration should be given to moving to electronic reporting as early as possible
context: print version divided into 3 volumes: Tabular list, Reference Guide, Index; all three are needed to use the ICD correctly
exception_condition: paper-based recording may cause problems with readability and timeliness of coded data
evidence_wording: It should be noted that paper-based recording requires manual transcription of the information into electronic systems and consideration should be given to moving to electronic reporting as early as possible in the information chain. ... The long-term goal for all users should be coding using ICD-11 in an electronic environment.

title: Electronic version
subject: ICD browser version and web services
object: retrieval of concepts by searching for terms, anatomy or any other element of the content model; user input reviewed annually
context: browser linked from https://icd.who.int; web services and browser allow access to all Tabular lists including mortality, morbidity, primary care, specialty linearisations
temporal_qualifier: input reviewed for consideration for inclusion on an annual basis
evidence_wording: The WHO provides this version for browsing ICD-11 in multiple languages (linked from https://icd.who.int). ... Both the web services and the online browser allow access and searching of all Tabular lists of the ICD, including for mortality and morbidity statistics, primary care, or for specialty linearisations for certain specific domains.

title: Links with other Classifications and Terminologies / Integrated use with Terminologies
subject: terminologies and classifications
object: complementary; ICD-11 Foundation is the terminological part of ICD-11 derived from the former ICD-10 Index and other sources
context: classifications have residual classes ('other specified' and 'unspecified') ensuring all cases can always be classified; third party terminologies ideally linked to ICD-11 Foundation in 1:1 or signposted 1:n relationships per the mapping paper
exception_condition: terminologies have no mechanism to report new information not previously added to the terminology
evidence_wording: Terminologies and classifications should be considered complementary. ICD-11 Foundation is the terminological part of ICD-11 derived from the former ICD-10 Index and other sources. Third party terminologies ideally are linked to the ICD-11 Foundation in 1:1 relationships or ‘signposted from ICD-11 foundation in 1:n relationships. These links shall follow the recommendations by the mapping paper.

title: Functioning in ICD and joint use with ICF overview
subject: ICD-11 functioning section
predicate: provides two options for impact assessment:
object: WHODAS 2.0 / Model Disability Survey (MDS) for an overall and domain specific functioning score; or a short-list of ICF Annex 9 functioning categories with a generic 5-point severity qualifier
context: signs and symptoms in ICD aligned with body functions in ICF; ICD takes an approach that identifies 'severity' as a property of the disease/disorder; wherever full functioning reporting is desired and required, the ICF should be used (see Section 2.11)
exception_condition: WHODAS 2.0 (like other clinical rating scales) has to be used as a whole (i.e. the full battery of questions) to obtain scores
evidence_wording: An optional functioning section has been embedded in ICD-11 to enable the classification and measurement of the impact of health conditions in terms of functioning. ... In order to obtain such scores, WHODAS 2.0 (like other clinical rating scales) has to be used as a whole (i.e. the full battery of questions). ... Wherever full functioning reporting is desired and required, the ICF should be used.

title: Structure and taxonomy of the ICD
subject: ICD chapter and block structure
object: 11 iterations of the classification over 150 years, balancing current knowledge against statistical comparability over space and time
context: chapters are not intended to delimit areas of medical expertise or domains of specialties; most widespread use of ICD is for cause of death (mortality) statistics
evidence_wording: The chapter and block structure of the ICD has evolved in 11 iterations of the classification over 150 years. ... Chapters are not intended to delimit areas of medical expertise or domains of specialties. The link to any specialty or reimbursement schemes is secondary.

title: Taxonomy
subject: statistical classification of diseases
object: a limited number of mutually exclusive categories able to encompass the complete range of morbid conditions; every disease must have a well-defined place
context: measures determining whether an entity qualifies to become a unique category: epidemiological evidence, clinical evidence, granularity, continuity, parsimony; residual categories exist for other and miscellaneous conditions; ICD-11 URIs allow retention of detail for future analysis
evidence_wording: A statistical classification of diseases must be confined to a limited number of mutually exclusive categories able to encompass the complete range of morbid conditions. ... The following measures apply in determining whether an entity qualifies to become a unique category: 1. Epidemiological evidence ... 2. Clinical evidence ... 3. Granularity ... 4. Continuity ... 5. Parsimony: the need to limit the number of categories for international mandatory reporting.

title: Content model and definition of disease
subject: disease (ICD-11 content model)
object: a set of dysfunctions in any body system defined by symptomatology/manifestations, aetiology, course and outcome, treatment response, linkage to genetic factors, linkage to environmental factors
context: for further information on the content model see 3.4 The Content Model
evidence_wording: A disease is usually defined using a set of relevant aspects drawn from the pattern below. A disease is a set of dysfunctions in any body system defined by: [table of properties: Symptomatology or manifestations; Aetiology; Course and outcome; Treatment response; Linkage to genetic factors; Linkage to environmental factors].

title: ICD Chapter structure
subject: ICD chapter structure ('special groups' chapters)
predicate: take priority over 'body systems' chapters when
object: there is any doubt as to where a condition should be positioned; enforced in the 'excludes' notes at the beginning of each chapter
context: ICD is a variable-axis classification derived from William Farr's structure; in general, conditions are primarily classified to one of the 'special groups' chapters
evidence_wording: Where there is any doubt as to where a condition should be positioned, the ‘special groups’ chapters take priority. This principle is enforced in the ‘excludes’ notes at the beginning of each chapter in the ICD.

title: Guiding principles for classification of special concepts
subject: placement of special concepts in ICD-11
object: clinical findings in Chapter 21; clinical manifestations in body system chapter (underlying condition has to be coded as well); syndromes of unknown aetiology with most relevant body system; 'due to' / 'multiple' / 'sequelae' / 'history of' categories restricted to exceptions; residual categories exist only where meaningful
context: acute postprocedural complications identified by combinations of codes from body system or injury chapters and external causes chapter
exception_condition: categories with mention of 'multiple' require coding of the different multiple conditions individually; 'sequelae' include residual effects specified as arrested, cured, healed, inactive, old or quiescent unless there is evidence of active disease
evidence_wording: The number of categories with ‘due to’ in the title are restricted to certain exceptions. ... Categories with mention of ‘multiple’ are restricted to exceptions and require coding of the different multiple conditions individually (e.g. multiple injuries are to be coded individually when possible). ... Residual categories exist only where they are meaningful.

title: General features of ICD-11 / Code structure
subject: ICD-11 stem codes
object: the range from 1A00.00 to ZZ9Z.ZZ; first character relates to the chapter number; a letter always in second position; letters O and I omitted; terminal Y reserved for 'other specified', terminal Z for 'unspecified' ('F'/'G' also used in chapters with more than 240 blocks)
context: main structural innovation: built on a Foundation Component from which Tabular lists are derived; codes starting with 'X' indicate an extension code (see 2.9); a dash in the Reference Guide indicates more detailed codes exist, e.g. 8B24- covers 8B24.0 to 8B24.Z
evidence_wording: The codes of the ICD–11 are alphanumeric and cover the range from 1A00.00 to ZZ9Z.ZZ. ... The letters ‘O’ and ‘I’ are omitted to prevent confusion with the numbers ‘0’ and ‘1’. ... The terminal letter Y is reserved for the residual category ‘other specified’ and the terminal letter ‘Z’ is reserved for the residual category ‘unspecified’.

title: Uniform resource identifiers
subject: Uniform Resource Identifier (URI)
object: a string of characters that uniquely identifies a particular ICD-11 entity; each entity has a specific place in the hierarchy of groups and categories
evidence_wording: All entities have a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) which is a string of characters that uniquely identifies a particular ICD-11 entity. Each entity has a specific place in the hierarchy of groups and categories.

title: Block codes
subject: ICD-11 blocks
object: reporting aggregated statistics; blocks do not have category codes as they are not supposed to be used in coding
context: blocks have their own URIs (e.g. Neoplasms http://id.who.int/icd/entity/1630407678) and block IDs 11 characters long (e.g. 'BlockL1-1A0')
exception_condition: blocks are not supposed to be used in coding
evidence_wording: Higher level entities in ICD-11 (called ‘blocks’) may be used for reporting aggregated statistics. However, blocks do not have category codes as they are not supposed to be used in coding. Blocks have their own URIs (e.g. the URI for Neoplasms is http://id.who.int/icd/entity/1630407678).

title: Stem codes
subject: stem codes
object: codes in the Tabular list of ICD-11 that can be used alone; designed to ensure meaningful information in use cases that require only one code per case
context: stem codes may be entities or groupings of high relevance in any of the use cases, or clinical conditions that should always be described as one single category
evidence_wording: Codes in the Tabular list of ICD-11 that can be used alone. Stem codes may be entities or groupings of high relevance in any of the use cases, or clinical conditions that should always be described as one single category. Stem codes are designed to ensure that in use cases that require only one code per case, meaningful information is collected.

title: Extension codes and postcoordination
subject: extension codes
predicate: are not to be used alone in the context of statistical classification but
object: must be added to a stem code; postcoordination links core diagnostic concepts (stem+stem) and/or extension codes into a cluster; permitted with all axes as long as at least one stem code is used
context: postcoordination is one of the significant changes compared with ICD-10; API, Browser and coding tool facilitate postcoordination in certain areas; refer to 2.9
exception_condition: extension codes may be used in another context, e.g. for device documentation; not all extension codes can be used with every stem code
evidence_wording: Extension codes are not to be used alone in the context of statistical classification but must be added to a stem code. ... Postcoordination is by matter of principle permitted with all axes, as long as at least one stem code is used.

title: Other general features
subject: ICD-11 category descriptions and special tabulation lists
object: short descriptions (maximum 100 words) in the Tabular list plus long 'additional information' descriptions without length restriction; special tabulation lists plus SMoL, verbal autopsy list, and infectious diseases by agent list
context: special tabulation lists refer to section 2.25; specialty linearisations allow representation of content from a specialty perspective
evidence_wording: ICD–11 categories have short descriptions, plus long descriptions labelled ‘additional information’. The short description is a maximum of 100 words ... Special tabulation lists (refer to section 2.25) continue to exist in ICD-11, but there are three additional lists - the Startup Mortality List (SMoL), the list for verbal autopsy, and the list for infectious diseases by agent.

title: Foundation Component and Tabular lists of ICD-11
subject: ICD-11 Foundation Component
object: a multidimensional collection of all ICD entities; an underlying database that holds all necessary information to generate print versions of the tabular list and the alphabetical index, specialty linearisations and country-specific modifications
context: in a Tabular list, entities become categories that are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive, linked to a mono hierarchical tree (only one parent); multiple-parent information remains available from the Foundation Component; several congruent tabular lists can be built from the same Foundation Component
evidence_wording: The Foundation Component is a multidimensional collection of all ICD entities. ... In a Tabular list, entities of the Foundation Component become categories. The categories are mutually exclusive and jointly exhaustive and linked to a mono hierarchical tree (that is, they have only one parent).

title: Precoordination and Postcoordination in ICD-11
subject: precoordination and postcoordination
object: precoordination: stem codes contain all pertinent information in a pre-combined fashion; postcoordination: combining multiple codes (two or more stem codes e.g. code1/code2, or stem code&extension code1&extension code2); the combination is called a cluster (refer to 2.10)
evidence_wording: A health condition may be described to any level of detail, by applying more than one code, or by ‘postcoordinating’ (i.e. combining): two or more stem codes, (e.g. code1/code2); stem codes with one or more extension codes. (e.g. stem code&extension code1&extension code2). ... The combination of codes is called a cluster. Refer to 2.10.

title: Multiple parenting
subject: multiple parenting
object: an entity to be correctly classified in two different places (e.g. by site or by aetiology); the decision about which place depends on international agreement and legacy
context: examples: oesophageal cancer (neoplasms vs digestive system); cerebral ischaemic conditions (vascular vs nervous system)
evidence_wording: An entity may be correctly classified in two different places, e.g. by site or by aetiology. For a disease, such as oesophageal cancer, this would mean that it could be classified to cancers (malignant neoplasms) or to conditions of the digestive system. ... A decision about which place a condition is in depends on international agreement and legacy.

title: Language independent ICD entities
subject: ICD-11 entities
object: language independent; the content model allows binding of any desired language to the elements of its Foundation Component
context: international maintenance handled in English; international translation base facilitates translations or multilingual browsing (See 3.12 Annex A)
evidence_wording: ICD-11 entities are language independent. The maintenance of the ICD-11 on an international level is handled in the English language but the content model of ICD–11 is language independent and allows binding of any desired language to the elements of its Foundation Component.

title: Main uses of the ICD: Mortality
subject: mortality statistics
object: medical research, monitoring of public health, evaluating health interventions, and planning and follow-up of health care; WHA rules standardise selection of a single cause for routine tabulation
context: implementation of the ICD for mortality requires infrastructure for reporting and storing information, design of information flows, quality assurance and feedback, and training
evidence_wording: Rules adopted by the World Health Assembly (WHA) regarding the selection of a single cause or condition, from death certificates, for routine tabulation of mortality statistics are provided to standardise production of mortality data.

title: What is coded: Causes of death
subject: underlying cause of death
object: (a) the disease or injury which initiated the train of morbid events leading directly to death, or (b) the circumstances of the accident or violence which produced the fatal injury
context: selected for routine single-cause tabulation of mortality statistics; effective public health interventions prevent harm or death by breaking the chain of events that lead to harm (See Section 2.21)
evidence_wording: the underlying cause of death has been defined as “(a) the disease or injury which initiated the train of morbid events leading directly to death, or (b) the circumstances of the accident or violence which produced the fatal injury”, and is selected for routine single-cause tabulation of mortality statistics.

title: Main uses of the ICD: Morbidity
subject: morbidity data
object: statistical reporting mostly at national or local levels; basis for casemix systems such as Diagnosis Related Groups (DRGs); inform clinical guidelines through Foundation Component information on burden of disease
evidence_wording: Morbidity data are used for statistical reporting mostly at national or local levels. ... ICD coded data also forms the basis for different casemix systems, such as different varieties of Diagnosis Related Groups (DRGs).

title: What is coded: patient conditions
subject: main condition
object: the one condition determined to be the reason for admission, established at the end of the episode of health care; the health care practitioner should record and identify it
context: the definition of main condition relates to the description of an episode of hospital-based care; the practitioner responsible for treatment is responsible for documenting conditions; clinical documentation is the starting point for coded health data (See Section 1.4)
evidence_wording: The health care practitioner should record and identify as the main condition the one condition that is determined to be the reason for admission, established at the end of the episode of health care. ... The importance of clinical documentation by health care practitioners as the starting point for coded health data cannot be overstated, and needs to be underlined as being a matter of key significance within countries and internationally.

title: Traditional Medicine
subject: Traditional Medicine (TM) chapter (TM1)
object: in conjunction with the Western Medicine concepts of ICD Chapters 1-25
context: international standardisation allows measuring, counting, comparing and monitoring over time; see 3.12 Annex A: ICD-11 Updating and Maintenance
exception_condition: the TM1 chapter is not designed to assess TM practice or the efficacy of any TM intervention
evidence_wording: It is recommended that coding of cases with ICD-11’s chapter on Traditional Medicine disorders and patterns (TM1) be used in conjunction with the Western Medicine concepts of ICD Chapters 1-25. As with other ICD chapters, the TM1 chapter is not designed to assess TM practice or the efficacy of any TM intervention.

title: ICD maintenance
subject: ICD maintenance process
object: updating of the ICD following evolution in understanding of diseases, treatments, and prevention; standardised open proposal and review mechanism on an online platform
context: workflows ensure proposed changes are considered from a medical and scientific perspective and from their value and place in a particular use case (See 3.12 Annex A)
evidence_wording: A standardised open process has been established to ensure that the proposed updates are collected, routed, reviewed, and duly considered before being implemented. A proposal and review mechanism on an online platform makes the process transparent.

title: Guiding principles of authoring process
subject: allocation of entities in the classification
predicate: follows rules in order of priority:
object: 1. no changes without rationale and documented change in aetiology or prevention method; 2. conditions classified predominantly by their aetiology; 3. conditions that could arguably be in two or more places remain in their legacy location; 4. keeping a group of subtypes together may override anatomical or aetiological considerations
context: e.g. Chapter 04 'Diseases of the immune system' added on sufficient scientific evidence; viral hepatitis in 'Certain infectious or parasitic disease'; human prion diseases kept together despite mixed components
exception_condition: where one condition can be due to multiple different aetiologies, and it is more relevant to retain the affected body system, it is usually classified with the body system
evidence_wording: No changes to the classification, including movement of categories or groups between chapters, without rationale and documented change in aetiology or prevention method. ... Conditions are classified predominantly by their aetiology. ... Conditions that could arguably be in two or more places of the classification remain in their legacy location. ... Keeping a group of subtypes together in one location may override anatomical or aetiological considerations.

title: Improving user guidance
subject: user guidance rules
object: add secondary parents where a condition could be in two or more places (creating a window with no primary children/terms/residual categories if needed); add an exclusion note for confusable conditions; create special linearisation lists for alternative tabulation; allow specialty linearisations (primary care, dermatology, neurology, ophthalmology, ICD-O, ICECI)
context: multiple parenting in the Foundation Component serves to address users expecting to find conditions in certain places; deprecated terms hidden from the ICD-11 browser (tabular) and not under 'All Index Terms'
evidence_wording: Where a condition could be in two or more places, identify these other places and add them as secondary parents ... Where a condition could be confused with another condition bearing a similar name, add an exclusion note. (e.g. ‘Influenza due to seasonal influenza virus’ has a note ‘Exclusion: Haemophilus influenzae [H. influenzae] meningitis’). ... Deprecated term: A term/concept that has been deemed invalid (outdated) for inclusion in the current version of ICD-11, which may still be recorded.

title: Introduction to the ICD-11 Update Process
subject: ICD-11 update process
predicate: is carried out at different levels with different frequencies:
object: continuous updates to Foundation Component and index entries; annual official releases ('blue browser'); every five years for updates impacting four- and five-character codes; every ten years for mortality and morbidity rules with significant statistical impact
context: any individual user can submit a proposal for an update; maintenance platform ('orange browser') used for proposals and comments; input requires proper referencing of sources, scientific evidence, and copyright permission
temporal_qualifier: annually / every five years / every ten years
evidence_wording: Continuous updates are made to the: ICD-11 Foundation Component; ICD-11 index entries. Official releases of the ICD-11 classification are produced: - Annually for international use in mortality and morbidity (known as the ‘blue browser’). Every five years for updates that impact on the four- and five-character codes. Every ten years for updates to the mortality and morbidity rules that have significant impact on statistical output.

title: National Modifications for morbidity coding
subject: national modifications of ICD-11
object: ideally agreed by ICD-11 maintenance bodies before national implementation; should not impact morbidity and mortality statistics and should not conflict with the foundation; approval subject to whether suitable detail already exists in the foundation; must incorporate changes to the international version as soon as possible; contractual arrangements with WHO required
context: example: 'Diabetes Type 1' is classified to 5A10 in the WHO version; a national modification could add 5A10.1 'Diabetes Type 1, uncontrolled', but when postcoordination provides the necessary detail a new subcategory may not be necessary
exception_condition: when the mechanism of postcoordination provides the necessary detail, the addition of a new subcategory may not be necessary
evidence_wording: All countries planning to produce national modifications must make relevant contractual arrangements with WHO. ... Modifications should not impact on morbidity and mortality statistics, and should not conflict with the foundation. ... If a change is made to the international version of ICD-11 the respective national modification must incorporate the change as soon as possible.

title: Part 2 - Using ICD-11 / Basic coding and reporting guidelines
subject: coding
object: the assignment of one or more codes in order to represent the meaning of a condition in as much detail as required
context: recommended to use the ICD-11 Smart coding tool (online and offline); print version option not recommended (time consuming, may cause confusion); if no electronic environment available, solutions in collaboration with WHO
exception_condition: Software must not include lists or other prompts to guide the recording or coding, as these necessarily limit the range of diagnoses and therefore have an adverse effect on the accuracy and usefulness of the record and report.
evidence_wording: Coding is the assignment of one or more codes in order to represent the meaning of a condition in as much detail as required. ... Software must not include lists or other prompts to guide the recording or coding, as these necessarily limit the range of diagnoses and therefore have an adverse effect on the accuracy and usefulness of the record and report.

title: Tabular List, Special Tabulation Lists, Qualifiers, and Modifiers
subject: ICD-11 Tabular list
object: an alphanumeric listing of diseases and disease groups, inclusion and exclusion notes, and some coding rules; Chapters 1 to 25 contain approximately 15 000 entities at the four-, five- or six-character level
context: special tabulation lists presented at the end of the Tabular list; not designed for coding but for tabulation and reporting only (2.25); extension codes (2.9) and Traditional medicine (1.5) sections exist in addition
exception_condition: Special tabulation lists are not designed for coding but are for tabulation and reporting only
evidence_wording: The Tabular list is an alphanumeric listing of diseases and disease groups, inclusion and exclusion notes, and some coding rules. Chapters 1 to 25 of the ICD contain approximately 15 000 entities at the four-, five- or six-character level. ... Special tabulation lists are not designed for coding but are for tabulation and reporting only (2.25).
